root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `consume_list()` uses the decoded list8 size to populate `subconsumer.size` and advance `consumer->position`, the selected list extent must not exceed `consumer->size - consumer->position`; the fixed code satisfies that obligation by clamping the selected extent with `scsize = min(s, consumer->size - consumer->position)`.
root_cause_criterion.description: On the crashing path, `consume_list()` reads `s == 0x20` after the two-byte `c0 20` list header, so `consumer->size - consumer->position == 0` before the subconsumer is formed. The vulnerable original still copies raw `s` into `subconsumer.size`, while the fixed original uses the clamped `scsize` for both `subconsumer.size` and the outer position advance, preventing the later count-byte dereference from relying on bytes that are not present.

nodes.state: After reading the attacker-controlled list8 size byte, `consume_list()` forms `*subconsumer` with `subconsumer->output_start == consumer->output_start + consumer->size`, so the new subconsumer starts at the end of the real described-value slice.

The `pni_consumer_readf8()` count-byte sink dereferences the same fabricated `subconsumer->output_start` as its read base, producing the AddressSanitizer-reported one-byte heap-buffer-overflow when that base already equals the end of the 5-byte allocation.

edges.relation: The extent selected by `consume_list()` becomes the exact logical `consumer->size` used by the later `pni_consumer_readf8()` count-byte read, so the vulnerable run checks that sink against the forged 32-byte extent instead of the zero real bytes remaining.
The fabricated base pointer created for `*subconsumer` in `consume_list()` becomes the exact `consumer->output_start` dereferenced when `pni_consumer_readf8()` fetches the list count byte.
